supported_claims.text: 车 is the modern simplified form of 車, adapted from its cursive form; the dossier reports that form by the Sui dynasty at the latest and its adoption as a standard character in 1956.

車 is a pictograph of a vehicle. Variable early forms depicted selected vehicle features such as wheels, body, axle, yoke, pole, or crossbar; later writing reduced and regularized those depictions. No component breakdown is warranted for this whole-graph pictograph.

Reported oracle-bone uses include vehicles and a place name; bronze uses include vehicles and war chariots. These reported examples lack calendar dates for the individual inscriptions, so they do not establish a precise earliest date or a sequence of meanings.

Dictionaries document later senses including wheeled machines, transporting by cart, and a cartload measure, but the dossier does not establish when these arose or a continuous semantic path from the vehicle sense.

disagreements.text: The whole spoken word represented by 車 has competing proposed external derivations, including Indo-Iranian comparisons; these proposals are disputed and do not establish the spoken name of the pictured vehicle. They concern the word, not a phonetic component in the graph.
The traditional account attributes the making of 車 to Xi Zhong in the Xia period, but the dossier presents this as a transmitted account, not independent confirmation.

limitations.text: The dossier supports a whole-graph pictographic analysis, not a semantic-phonetic compound; therefore no phonetic component or component sound comparison applies.
The individual early inscription examples are identified by corpus numbers but are not given calendar dates in the inspected evidence.
The sources list later meanings but do not establish their chronology or the links between them.
The curated historical glyphs are modern vector redrawings, not artifact photographs, and their pixels were not visually inspected in the supplied research.
